_purpose: Per-CUSIP Cal-Mortgage insurance status for the 4 CHFFA hospital revenue bond holdings in the ETF basket. Verification method: cross-reference each underlying obligor against the HCAI Cal-Mortgage Loan Insurance Program Monthly Activity Report 'Insured Loans by Borrower' table (most recent: ending June 30, 2025).
_verification_source_supplementary: SEC EDGAR NPORT-P filings (cross-reference obligor identity for opaque CHFFA labels)
_hostile_validator_rules: If the Cal-Mortgage Monthly Activity Report does not list the underlying obligor by name in the Insured Loans table, mark NOT_INSURED.
If the underlying obligor identity cannot be confirmed from a primary source (OS PDF, NPORT-P with explicit title), mark obligor_identification_confidence: MEDIUM and flag for re-verification.

Do not assume a CHFFA-issued bond is Cal-Mortgage insured. CHFFA is a conduit issuer; Cal-Mortgage is a separate HCAI insurance program with a finite ~55-loan portfolio dominated by small CCRCs, clinics, and district hospitals.

holdings.cal_mortgage_verification_method: El Camino Hospital does NOT appear in the HCAI Cal-Mortgage Loan Insurance Program Monthly Activity Report 'Insured Loans by Borrower' table as of June 30, 2025. The bond carries native AA/Aa3 ratings consistent with the underlying hospital's standalone credit, not the State of California AA- Cal-Mortgage wrap.
holdings.framework_verdict: NAKED_OPERATOR_CREDIT — operator-credit detectors apply directly; no Cal-Mortgage masking layer.

holdings.obligor_identification_source: SEC EDGAR Invesco Exchange-Traded Fund Trust II NPORT-P (filing 0001378872-26-000865, period 2026-02-28): title field reads 'California (State of) Health Facilities Financing Authority (Stanford Health Care), Series 2025, RB' for CUSIP 13032U3Y2.
holdings.cal_mortgage_verification_method: Stanford Health Care does NOT appear in the HCAI Cal-Mortgage Loan Insurance Program Monthly Activity Report 'Insured Loans by Borrower' table as of June 30, 2025. Stanford is a $20B+ revenue multi-hospital system with native A1/A+ credit — Cal-Mortgage is structurally designed for small/standalone facilities that cannot otherwise access investment-grade muni markets.
holdings.framework_verdict: NAKED_OPERATOR_CREDIT — Stanford's AA- rating reflects its own consolidated credit, not a wrap. Operator-credit detectors apply naked.

holdings.underlying_obligor: Providence St. Joseph Health (Providence Health & Services)
holdings.cal_mortgage_verification_method: Providence St. Joseph Health does NOT appear in the HCAI Cal-Mortgage Loan Insurance Program Monthly Activity Report 'Insured Loans by Borrower' table as of June 30, 2025. Providence is a 51-hospital multi-state Catholic health system; CHFFA conduit issuance reflects Providence's own A/A3 credit, not a wrap.
holdings.framework_verdict: NAKED_OPERATOR_CREDIT — discount bond at 3% reflects coupon-vs-current-market pricing dynamic; credit signal is Providence-system level (operating margin deterioration 2023-2025 is on-credit, not wrap-masked).

holdings.cal_mortgage_verification_method: Adventist Health System/West does NOT appear in the HCAI Cal-Mortgage Loan Insurance Program Monthly Activity Report 'Insured Loans by Borrower' table as of June 30, 2025. Adventist Health is a 20+ hospital system; the BBB+ rating reflects its own standalone credit profile, not a wrap (a wrapped bond would carry State of California AA- credit, not BBB+).
holdings.framework_verdict: NAKED_OPERATOR_CREDIT — at BBB+ this is the most credit-exposed of the four. Cascade detector does not apply, but operator-credit detectors (covenant_tripwire, hcai_seismic, going_concern, coverage_ratio_thin) should fire if conditions warrant. NB: BBB+ at 3% coupon is a discount bond — current YTM will reflect both credit spread AND market-rate-vs-coupon dynamics.

summary.framework_alpha_applies: NO — all 4 holdings are naked operator credit. Cal-Mortgage cascade signal (St. Rose Hospital ~$13.96M new pipeline default Q1 2025) does NOT affect ETF holdings because no holding is wrapped.
summary.etf_rebalancing_implication: If ETF were a Cal-Mortgage-wrapped CA NH/CCRC basket, the May 2025 St. Rose Hospital cascade would weaken the wrap and re-introduce operator credit signal. Because the ETF holds only large unwrapped multi-system credits (Stanford, Providence, El Camino, Adventist), the cascade signal is structurally irrelevant. The framework's value-add on this basket comes from operator-credit detectors directly applied to each obligor, not from cascade monitoring.
